column1: # Shared aontu unit tests: the `+` OPERAND CROSS-PRODUCT. Columns
# mode: canon = unify(src).canon == expect ; err = generate(src) errors,
# THE WHOLE TABLE, IN ONE PLACE. `+` is aontu's only binary operator and
# the number tower (docs/design/number-tower.md, D6) gives it four
# numeric leaves to promote between, so the promotion surface is now a
# 6x6 table: integer, float, biginteger, bigdecimal, string and boolean,
# in BOTH operand orders. The tower's own risk register calls for pinning
# it exhaustively ("the promotion table is small and closed; pin the full
# operand-pair cross-product as spec rows"), with boru's
# lang/spec/numeric-cross-product.tsv as the template. This is that file.
# Every row below was derived by the parity probe: the source was run
# through BOTH engines and only a result they agreed on, byte for byte,
# was written down. A handful of pairs are also pinned as design-contract
# rows in number-tower.tsv; the duplication is deliberate. That file
# argues one decision at a time, this one is the closed table, and a
# table with holes in it is not a table.
# CANON IS THE MODE. The point of nearly every row here is which KIND the
# result has, and `gen` cannot see a kind (see docs/shared-spec.md). Where
# a pair is refused, the row is `err` on a substring both ports produce.
# THE OPERANDS, one per kind, chosen so every result below is distinct:
# ROW 1 -- INTEGER on the left. It is the one leaf on BOTH ladders: the
# exact ladder (integer < biginteger < bigdecimal) and float's classic
# contagion, which is why `1+2.0` is a float and `1+0d2` a biginteger.
# ROW 2 -- FLOAT on the left. Float is OFF the exact ladder: it mixes
# with integer and with itself, and meeting either Big leaf is a hard
# ROW 3 -- BIGINTEGER on the left. The exact ladder promotes to the
# WIDEST operand, so a biginteger absorbs an integer and is absorbed by a
# ROW 4 -- BIGDECIMAL on the left, the any of the exact ladder: it
# absorbs both other exact leaves and never demotes back (`0d0.5+0d0.5`
# ROW 5 -- STRING on the left. A string operand wins over every other
# kind, boolean included, and the other operand contributes its DIGITS:
# no `0d` marker, no kind decoration. Note `float-plus-str` and
# `bigint-plus-str` above land on the same "2q" from different leaves --
# concatenation is deliberately blind to kind.
# ROW 6 -- BOOLEAN on the left. Boolean has its own rule: boolean with
# boolean is logical OR, boolean with a string concatenates, and boolean
# with any NUMBER does not coerce at all (there is no 0/1 in this
# language) -- the op is simply left unresolved, in either order.
# WHAT AN UNRESOLVED `+` DOES. The twelve boolean-with-number cells above
# are pinned by canon, which shows the op surviving unresolved. That is
# only half the behaviour: the other half is that such a value cannot be
# generated, and says so. One row per direction is enough -- the canon
# rows above already pin that the whole diagonal band behaves alike.
# THE COLUMN THE TABLE DOES NOT HAVE: a NON-SCALAR operand. Kinds, null,
# lists, maps and any are not operands at all, and an exact leaf does not
# change that -- the op stays unresolved exactly as it does for an
# integer (plus.tsv:top-operand-err is the landed integer case). These
# matter because a `*big.Int` or a `Decimal` reaching a coercion path
# would be the silent corruption D6 exists to prevent, so the refusal is
# THE DIGITS RULE, IN FULL. String concatenation renders the number's
# digits and nothing else -- and the surprise is that "nothing else" is
# not the same string for a float and for a bigdecimal of the same value.
# A float drops an integral fraction (`1.0` concatenates as "1", the
# landed JS-parity rule), while a BIGDECIMAL keeps the one decimal place
# that IS its plain form: an integral bigdecimal has no other rendering,
# because `0d1000` would be a different lattice point (a biginteger).
# So the `.0` that never leaks out of a float does appear for a
# bigdecimal, and the two rows below sit next to each other so that the
# difference is a decision on the record rather than an accident.
# A chain that ends in a string: the numbers add on the exact ladder
# first and only the final value is rendered, so the marker never
# appears even though two exact leaves took part.
